doc: The current conventions' inference-details record, `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details`: one event or log record per model call carrying the whole call - its system instruction, its request and its response - as attributes. A container, not a message: its attributes are the messages, so its raw form is replaced by what is read from it. Apart from `semconv` because it is one self-contained construct; its clause ids keep that asset's namespace because they are the conventions' own.

carriers.doc: The same instruction carried by the inference-details event (`semconv.event_inference_details_system`): the attribute's meaning on the event that reports the request, so a detached frame of that request whichever carrier the producer chose.

messages.doc: The system instruction the same container carries, as the conventions write it on a span (`semconv.system_instructions`): a parts array, wrapped under `parts`. Without it the container's request lost its instruction - the details event replaces its raw form, so an attribute no reading names is read by nothing. Before the input (29 < 30), so the instruction heads the request it was sent with.

The convention's inference-details event is a *container*: its own attributes are the request and the response, so the container itself is not a message - reporting it as well would give the conversation twice. Read on a tool span too: the retired extractor answered this event before any tool-span check.

The response side of the same container. Read on a tool span too: the retired extractor answered this event before any tool-span check. After `google-adk.operation_details_output` (31), which reads the same carrier element by element where the elements state a stream's parts, and leaves it whole to this rule everywhere else.

message_events.name: gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details
message_events.doc: A container whose own attributes are the request and the response.

log_events.name: gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details
log_events.doc: The inference-details container as a log record: its own attributes are the request and the response, read by the same container readings as the span event.
